newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Hirsch Int'l sees EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Hirsch Int'l sees EPS growth.

text.p: Hirsch International Corp Chief Financial Officer Kenneth Shifrin on Monday said he was comfortable with estimates that the company would post earnings per share of $0.28 for the fourth quarter and $1.09 for the year ending January 31, reflecting recent acquisitions.

Shifrin, who was interviewed along with Chairman, President and Chief Executive Harvey Arnberg, said the distributor of embroidery machinery expected 20 percent revenue growth in the year ending January 1998. He said he was comfortable with an earnings estimate of $1.32 per share for that period.

Hirsch reported earnings per share of $0.23 for the previous fourth quarter and $0.87 for the previous fiscal year, reflecting a five-for-four stock split. Annual revenues for the 1996 fiscal year totaled about $88 million.

Arnberg said the company would focus its growth efforts in the sales territories it picked up in 1996 through the acquisitions of Sedeco Inc and Sewing Machine Exchange Inc. Hirsch is making inroads into Latin America and Europe, Arnberg said.
The acquisitions expanded Hirsch's distribution of Japan-based Tajima Industries Ltd's embroidery machines.

Hirsch offers a variety of Tajima's machines. The range extends from equipment for small businesses costing about $20,000 to machines for textile factories that could embroider 30 objects at the same time, Arnberg said. An example of a larger machine is a $115,000 machine that embroiders 18 caps at a time, Arnberg said.

Growth in employee uniforms, professional sports team logos, brand-name products, high fashion apparel, automotive use and screen printing are expected to spur demand for Hirsch's equipment, Arnberg said.
In addition, Arnberg said software to operate the machines, supplies and leasing were also contributing to its profitability.
